title: Most anesthetics in plants and animals are gap junction uncouplers

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Most anesthetics in plants and animals are gap junction uncouplers

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Most anesthetics that remove cognition and sensory experience, in both plants and animals, act as gap junctional (bioelectric) uncouplers, which the author takes as consistent with connectivity binding cells into larger Selves.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It is thus no coincidence that most anesthetics used to remove cognition and sensory experience, whether in plants or animals, are gap junctional (bioelectric) uncouplers (Mantz et al., 1993; Wentlandt et al., 2006; Liu et al., 2012; Gremiaux et al., 2014; Baluska et al., 2016).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity”. Scope: General and volatile anesthetics used in plants and animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-18: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The majority claim is directly checkable against public pharmacology and literature-linked assay data. Coverage is imperfect, especially for plants, but a systematic analysis can confirm or refute the stated generalization.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compile commonly used plant and animal anesthetics, quantify evidence that each uncouples gap junctions at anesthetic concentrations, and test whether a majority meet that criterion relative to appropriate non-anesthetic compounds.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Gap-junction effects may occur only above clinically relevant concentrations.

Plant anesthesia and cognition are contested categories.

fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.55

analysis feasibility: 0.72
discriminating power: 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The generalization is a fraction over a definable drug list, with coupling as the assay. The Guide to Pharmacology holds the ligand list and some connexin interactions, and the coupling measurements themselves are spread through primary papers. A compilation can test the animal volatile agents that have been assayed and will miss much of the plant half. Multiple targets mean a positive uncoupling result does not show that uncoupling is how anesthesia happens, which the claim treats as support for a binding theory. The fraction is partly compilable now.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fix a list of general and volatile anesthetics used in animals and in plants, and score each for a dye-transfer or scrape-loading reduction of gap-junction coupling. 'Most' is confirmed if a pre-specified majority reduce coupling in both kingdoms; a majority with no coupling effect, especially among plant anesthetics, would refute the generalization.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A drug can close gap junctions and still act clinically through another target.

Gap-junction uncoupling is not a structured field for most anesthetics.

Plant anesthesia data are much sparser than mammalian data.

fields.label: Dimension scores

analysis feasibility: 0.48
data adequacy: 0.38
